cards.public_summary: Baker Mayfield agreed to a new four-year contract that keeps him under contract with Tampa Bay through 2029.
cards.evidence: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Baker Mayfield have agreed on a new four-year contract with a three-year extension that locks in one of the most productive quarterbacks in the NFL through the 2029 season and makes him the highest-paid player in franchise history. Through his first three seasons (2023-25) as the Buccaneers' starting quarterback, Mayfield ranks second in the NFL in touchdown passes (95) and third in passing yards (12,237) and has led the team to a pair of division championships.
cards.commentary: Mayfield's long-term deal reinforces his stability as Tampa Bay's quarterback, with no immediate change to his expected role or workload.
cards.author: Scott Smith

cards.public_summary: Baker Mayfield and the Buccaneers resolved their offseason contract dispute and completed an extension, River Wells reported.
cards.evidence: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Baker Mayfield had a bit of a contract spat over the offseason, with neither side able to get an extension done from free agency all the way to the end of training camp. Now, that spat is over.
cards.commentary: The new deal removes Mayfield's contract uncertainty heading into the season. It does not by itself establish any change to his role, workload or fantasy projection.
cards.author: River Wells
